speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; let's start by asking how long these symptoms have been present and if you have any history of recent travel or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That 3-day history of wrist pain, chills, and malaise following a camping trip in Minnesota raises concern for Lyme disease or Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. Did you notice a rash, particularly on your wrists or ankles, or any tick bites during your trip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erysipelas (or potentially Cellulitis) of the left wrist, likely secondary to a minor unnoticed trauma from camping. The description of "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" and significant swelling/erythema is characteristic of a bacterial skin infection. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and Blood Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Photo of wrist lesions and swelling.
